title: Extended narrative and speech
prior_teaching_boundary: Only the fifteen active contracts and actual registers at e1d94be establish teaching. Recognition and supplied exposure remain distinct from production; no archived milestones are inherited.
productive_outcomes: Produce every productive position of the complete selected nominal, adjectival and verbal systems, using their actual diagnostic stems, endings, exceptions and expressly bounded senses; preserve recognition-only, supplied and reference-only positions within their stated scope.
Preserve subjects, objects, recipients and relative internal cases across extended clauses; distinguish perception actors with infinitives from nominative subjects of finite content clauses.
Trace participants across quotation, reported content and narrated execution; recognize genuine ambiguity and use explicit nouns when an output requires unambiguous reference.
Interpret simultaneous, anterior and intended-later situations from complete verb groups and context without automatic English backshift or an automatic future auxiliary.

Use the newly assigned personal-acquaintance sense of cunnan, the separately evidenced personal-object witan, substitute-action dōn and bounded adverbial action comparison; do not impose an exclusive persons/facts division on the knowing verbs.
Use each additional explicitly taught lexical government or complement frame required by Cook32–36, keeping complete local helps visible for dependencies deliberately left supplied.

Translate all59 unchanged Cook prompts with every clause, participant, lexical hint, omission and word-order control accounted for; distinguish linguistic validity from compliance with an explicit target.
recognition_outcomes: Translate the complete444word gymnasium scene with its local support, preserving arrival, announcement, game, recognition, service, departure, inquiry and invitation.
Analyse the selected source pronouns, clause relations, finite and nonfinite forms, moods and relative temporal viewpoints without assigning productive mastery from a supplied token.
Explain the final source mixture of direct and indirect construction through its actual speaker, immediate addressee and intended message recipient.

Identify the edition's stated uncertainties in the king's knowledge/equal clause and the top passage, using supplied English explanations of the Latin parallels while translating the actual Old English.
bounded_scope: The actual fifteen-unit contracts and registers at e1d94be alone establish prior teaching. A prior headword, source exposure or complete table does not license an untaught sense, use or unassigned mood.
New nominal systems using familiar prior classes retain the stated count, mass, abstract, title and proper-name limits. No number sense or defective position is invented to fill a rectangle.

All newly introduced verbal systems are complete within their stated indicative, present-subjunctive, imperative or nonfinite scope; citation principal parts do not silently create other moods or syntax.
The new nearu adjective system retains its u/w alternation and complete strong/weak positive morphology. The new both system is plural; it does not acquire invented singular forms.
Cunnan and witan have overlapping lexical possibilities. The selected complement contrast is a bounded teaching target, not an exclusive persons-versus-facts rule.

Source-specific, rare and deliberately supplied Cook constructions remain supported during assessment. Their exact form, sense and whole-frame records must all be bound; no supplied help is tested as unaided recall.
The exact reading ends at170.16 tō his gereorde. Earlier Apollonius readings and the following feast are not silently reassigned.

The reading retains every original note and anchor. Its missing closing speech mark and ambiguous constructions are explained separately rather than silently normalized into a different Old English text.
Every new composition is declared teaching material. Every requested output has an explicit target, essential meaning, defensible alternatives and relevant error diagnosis before the prose gate.
Four short translated examples precede the corresponding practice after their prerequisites; there is no additional invented narrative.
audited_inflection_rules: Nouns of a previously taught class are explicitly derived from verified shared models; a complete paradigm does not grant unassigned senses or syntax.
Mass/abstract/proper-title sense inventories do not invent count plurals.
All old IDs and source analyses are preserved; contextual analyses may add a task-specific interpretation without erasing earlier records.
audit_recommendation_precedence: This reconciled contract assigns teaching. Audit proposals supply evidence; complete morphology does not establish every sense or construction.

source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Æfter ðisum wordum hē ēode on ðone weg ðe him
getǣht[1] wæs, ōð-ðæt hē becōm tō ðǣre ceastre geate, and
ðǣr inēode. Mid-ðȳ-ðe hē ðōhte hwone hē biddan meahte
līfes fultumes,[2] ðā geseah hē ǣnne nacodne cnapan geond
ðā strǣte iernan. Sē wæs mid[3] ęle gesmierwed, and mid
scīetan begyrd, and bær geongra[4] manna[4] plegan[4] on handa,
tō ðǣm bæðstęde[5] belimpende.[6] And cleopode[7] micelre
stefne,[8] and cwæð: “Gehīere,[9] gē ceasterwaran[10]! Gehīere,
gē ęlðēodige,[11] frige and ðēowe, æðele and unæðele! Se
bæðstęde is open.”
Ðā-ðā Apollonius ðæt gehīerde, hē hine unscrȳdde ðǣm[12]
healfan sciccelse ðe hē on hæfde, and ēode intō ðǣm ðwēale.[13]
And mid-ðȳ-ðe hē behēold hiera ānra[14] gehwilcne on hiera
weorce, hē sōhte his gelīcan,[15] ac hē ne meahte hine ðǣr
findan on ðǣm flocce. Ðā fǣringa cōm Arcestrates, ealre
ðǣre ðēode[16] cyning,[17] mid micelre męnige his manna,[18] and
inēode on ðæt bæð. Ðā āgan se cyning plegian wið[19] his
gefērum mid ðoðore.[20] And Apollonius hine[21] gemęngde,[21]
swā-swā God wolde, on ðæs cyninges plegan, and, iern-
ende, ðone ðoðor gelæhte,[1] and, mid swiftre hrædnesse
geslægene,[2] ongēan gesęnde tō ðǣm plegiendan cyninge.
Ęft hē āgēan āsęnde; hē hrædlīce slōh, swā hē hine[3]
nǣfre feallan ne lēt. Se cyning ðā oncnēow ðæs geongan
snelnesse,[4] ðæt hē wiste[5] ðæt hē næfde his gelīcan on
ðǣm plegan.[6] Ðā cwæð hē tō his gefērum: “Gāð ēow
heonan; ðes cniht, ðæs-ðe mē ðyncð,[7] is mīn gelīca.”
Ðā-ðā Apollonius gehīerde ðæt se cyning hine hęrede,
hē arn hrædlīce, and genēalǣcte tō ðǣm cyninge, and
mid gelǣredre[8] handa[9] hē swang[10] ðone top mid swā
micelre swiftnesse ðæt ðǣm cyninge wæs geðūht swilce
hē of ielde tō geoguðe gewęnd wǣre. And, æfter ðǣm,
on his cynesętle hē him[11] gecwēmlīce[12] ðēnode[13]; and,
ðā-ðā hē ūtēode of ðǣm bæðe, hē[14] hine[15] lǣdde be ðǣre
handa, and him[16] ðā siððan ðanan gewęnde, ðæs weges[17]
ðe hē ǣr cōm.
Ðā cwæð se cyning tō his mannum,[1] siððan Apollonius
āgān[2] wæs: “Ic swęrie ðurh ðā gemǣnan hǣle[3] ðæt ic
mē nǣfre bęt ne baðode ðonne ic dyde[4] tō-dæg, nāt ic
ðurh[5] hwilces geonges mannes ðēnunge.[6] Ðā beseah hē
hine tō ānum his manna, and cwæð: “Gā, and gewite
hwæt[7] se geonga mann sīe, ðe mē tō-dæg swā wel gehīer-
sumode.”
Se mann ðā ēode æfter Apollonio. Mid-ðȳ-ðe hē geseah
ðæt hē[8] wæs mid horgum[9] sciccelse bewǣfed, ðā węnde
hē ongēan tō ðǣm cyninge, and cwæð: “Se geonga mann
ðe[10] ðū æfter āscodest is forliden[11] mann.[11]” Ðā cwæð se
cyning: “Ðurh[12] hwæt[12] wāst[13] ðū ðæt?” Se mann him
andswarode, and cwæð: “Ðēah hē hit self forswīge,[14] his
gegierela hine gesweotolað.” Ðā cwæð se cyning: “Gā
hrædlīce, and sęge him ðæt[15] ‘se cyning bitt ðē ðæt ðū
cume[16] tō his gereorde.’”

Mid-ðȳ-ðe hē ðōhte hwone hē biddan meahte līfes fultumes, ðā geseah hē ǣnne nacodne cnapan geond ðā strǣte iernan. Sē wæs mid ęle gesmierwed, and mid scīetan begyrd, and bær geongra manna plegan on handa, tō ðǣm bæðstęde belimpende. And cleopode micelre stefne, and cwæð: “Gehīere, gē ceasterwaran! Gehīere, gē ęlðēodige, frige and ðēowe, æðele and unæðele! Se bæðstęde is open.”

Ðā-ðā Apollonius ðæt gehīerde, hē hine unscrȳdde ðǣm healfan sciccelse ðe hē on hæfde, and ēode intō ðǣm ðwēale. And mid-ðȳ-ðe hē behēold hiera ānra gehwilcne on hiera weorce, hē sōhte his gelīcan, ac hē ne meahte hine ðǣr findan on ðǣm flocce. Ðā fǣringa cōm Arcestrates, ealre ðǣre ðēode cyning, mid micelre męnige his manna, and inēode on ðæt bæð. Ðā āgan se cyning plegian wið his gefērum mid ðoðore. And Apollonius hine gemęngde, swā-swā God wolde, on ðæs cyninges plegan, and, iernende, ðone ðoðor gelæhte, and, mid swiftre hrædnesse geslægene, ongēan gesęnde tō ðǣm plegiendan cyninge. Ęft hē āgēan āsęnde; hē hrædlīce slōh, swā hē hine nǣfre feallan ne lēt. Se cyning ðā oncnēow ðæs geongan snelnesse, ðæt hē wiste ðæt hē næfde his gelīcan on ðǣm plegan. Ðā cwæð hē tō his gefērum: “Gāð ēow heonan; ðes cniht, ðæs-ðe mē ðyncð, is mīn gelīca.”

Ðā-ðā Apollonius gehīerde ðæt se cyning hine hęrede, hē arn hrædlīce, and genēalǣcte tō ðǣm cyninge, and mid gelǣredre handa hē swang ðone top mid swā micelre swiftnesse ðæt ðǣm cyninge wæs geðūht swilce hē of ielde tō geoguðe gewęnd wǣre. And, æfter ðǣm, on his cynesętle hē him gecwēmlīce ðēnode; and, ðā-ðā hē ūtēode of ðǣm bæðe, hē hine lǣdde be ðǣre handa, and him ðā siððan ðanan gewęnde, ðæs weges ðe hē ǣr cōm.

Ðā cwæð se cyning tō his mannum, siððan Apollonius āgān wæs: “Ic swęrie ðurh ðā gemǣnan hǣle ðæt ic mē nǣfre bęt ne baðode ðonne ic dyde tō-dæg, nāt ic ðurh hwilces geonges mannes ðēnunge. Ðā beseah hē hine tō ānum his manna, and cwæð: “Gā, and gewite hwæt se geonga mann sīe, ðe mē tō-dæg swā wel gehīersumode.”

Se mann ðā ēode æfter Apollonio. Mid-ðȳ-ðe hē geseah ðæt hē wæs mid horgum sciccelse bewǣfed, ðā węnde hē ongēan tō ðǣm cyninge, and cwæð: “Se geonga mann ðe ðū æfter āscodest is forliden mann.” Ðā cwæð se cyning: “Ðurh hwæt wāst ðū ðæt?” Se mann him andswarode, and cwæð: “Ðēah hē hit self forswīge, his gegierela hine gesweotolað.” Ðā cwæð se cyning: “Gā hrædlīce, and sęge him ðæt ‘se cyning bitt ðē ðæt ðū cume tō his gereorde.’”
source_spans.line_number_convention: Editorial count of Old English text lines from the first prose line on each printed page, anchored by printed marginal multiples of five. Individual line numbers are not all printed.

modern_support.source_phrase: ōð-ðæt hē becōm
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Until he arrived: an endpoint clause; retain the source macron.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: hwone hē biddan meahte līfes fultumes
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: hwone is the person asked, while līfes fultumes names the requested support of life. meahte can be indicative or subjunctive in form; context is a question within his thought, not proof of a uniquely recognizable ending.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: geseah hē ǣnne nacodne cnapan ... iernan
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Accusative participant with a perception infinitive. Cook’s glossary allows nacod to mean wearing only a tunic here; do not require a claim of total nudity.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: geongra manna plegan ... tō ðǣm bæðstęde belimpende
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: plegan literally denotes play/games; carrying equipment for the young men’s games is a contextual explanation, not a new unrestricted dictionary sense. belimpende modifies plegan, as note6 says; it is not another finite action of the boy.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: Gehīere, gē ceasterwaran ...
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: The call is addressed to the plural audience. Supply the whole source exhortation; do not replace its Gehīere with a silently regularized imperative.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: hine unscrȳdde ðǣm healfan sciccelse ðe hē on hæfde
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Reflexive undressing and the garment in the dative; the relative clause says he had the cloak on. Preserve the source construction as a whole.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: hiera ānra gehwilcne on hiera weorce
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Each single one of them at their work: first hiera participates in the partitive expression; second is possessive. Keep the printed short spelling.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: mid swiftre hrædnesse geslægene
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Cook note2 remarks on the participle’s awkward form. Supply the complete phrase as describing the ball struck with swift speed; retain geslægene rather than silently repairing agreement.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: oncnēow ... ðæt hē wiste ðæt hē næfde his gelīcan
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: The nested reference is unclear, as Cook note6 states. næfde is negative: the text does not say he had an equal. The Latin comparison concerns the king’s previously unmatched skill; use it as help while retaining the OE uncertainty, not as an invisible replacement text.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: ðæs-ðe mē ðyncð
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: As it seems to me: exact parenthetic impersonal construction, dative experiencer mē.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: swang ... ðone top ... swilce ... gewęnd wǣre
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Retain the OE’s throwing/striking of the top, tentatively a ball. Cook’s Latin comparison means rubbing him with ointment and the rejuvenating effect. No shoulder/neck noun occurs. Learners need this English explanation, not independent Latin translation. wǣre belongs to the imagined transformation comparison.

modern_support.source_phrase: him ... hē hine lǣdde be ðǣre handa ... him ... gewęnde
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Keep the original notes11,14–16 available for the pronoun chain. The later him is reflexive; the by-the-hand phrase specifies how one person leads another.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: ðæs weges ðe hē ǣr cōm

modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: siððan Apollonius āgān wæs
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: After Apollonius had gone away: intransitive completed departure with be, not a passive in which someone sends him away.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: ðurh ðā gemǣnan hǣle
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Oath by the common safety/salvation; welfare is an explanatory contextual alternative. hǣle is feminine accusative singular of hǣlu, reusing the older exact source form and safety/rescue sense. No possessive our is printed.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: ðurh hwilces geonges mannes ðēnunge ... hwæt se geonga mann sīe
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: The service is the means of the benefit; hwilces ... mannes is its genitive dependent. hwæt asks what sort/status of man he is. sīe is the dependent interrogative be form.
modern_support.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

modern_support.source_phrase: ēode æfter Apollonio ... ðe ðū æfter āscodest
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Going after a person, then asking about him: the relative marker is the complement of æfter within the clause; do not force temporal after for either use.

modern_support.source_phrase: Ðēah hē hit self forswīge
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Concessive clause: even if he himself keeps it unspoken. Supply the source forswīge with its present subjunctive interpretation; do not demand a full new weak-verb paradigm.

modern_support.source_phrase: sęge him ðæt ‘se cyning bitt ðē ðæt ðū cume ...’
modern_support.actual_supplied_text: Cook note15 explicitly diagnoses mixed direct/reported construction. First him is the messenger’s addressee; within the quoted message ðē is the person invited (accusative), and ðū/cume address him directly. Retain wording and speech levels; no silent repair.

verbal_glossary.explanation: Past participle in passive getǣht wæs; him is the person to whom the route was indicated.
Prefixed movement verb; do not split into an unnoticed new finite gān spelling.
Inside the dependent question hwone ... biddan meahte; indicative/subjunctive surface coincides. The selected interpretation is possibility in the thought.
Exact source prefixed participle and retained w; distinct from selected unprefixed smierwan paradigm. Mid ęle marks the anointing material.
Passive/predicative participle with mid scīetan, a cloth.
Tō + dative bæðstęde identifies what the games/equipment relate to; preserve source note6.
The new productive cry sense; micelre stefne is a dative of manner/instrument.
Exact plural command with shortened -e before following gē, not singular by surface alone. The same form recurs later in the line.
Hine is the person undressed; ðǣm healfan sciccelse is the removed clothing, supplied case frame.
Accusative persons observed; no modern behold quotation formula implied.
On ðæt bæð gives the entry destination.
StrongIII preterite of āginnan, not āgan own/possess and not āgān depart.
Infinitive after began; wið + dative companions and mid + dative ball are supported locally.
Reflexive hine; on ðæs cyninges plegan continues on 169.1. Plegan is an oblique noun governed by on; ðæs cyninges is its genitive possessor. It is not a finite verb.
Joined across printed line break iern-/ende; the supplied participle accompanies Apollonius. Do not count the two printed fragments as two words.
Exact source preterite has short æ as printed; preserve lexical spelling and do not silently import a guessed long form.
Exact accusative participle agreeing with ðone ðoðor, an evidenced exceptional -e form noted by Cook; do not regularize to a new target.
Tō + dative recipient; ongēan is the return direction.
Weak dative modifier of cyninge after ðǣm; the finite paradigm does not itself teach this participial cell.
Exact source singular h spelling; Wright262–263 explicitly gives slōg/slōh. Preserve the earlier selected slōg system and supply this contextual variant.
Accusative snelnesse, followed by a result/content sequence whose pronoun referents remain genuinely underdetermined in Cook note6.
Accusative hine is the praised person; the exact source spelling remains.
New productive selected preterite.
The prefixed verb with tō + dative goal is supplied; do not rename it as the unprefixed nēalǣcan form.

Direct object top is the actual Old English object. The Latin parallel describes rubbing or anointing with ointment; it contains no shoulder or neck noun. Keep that separate event distinct from the Old English.
Supply ðǣm cyninge wæs geðūht swilce ... wǣre, it seemed to the king as though ...; dative experiencer and irrealis comparison are explicit.
In swilce hē of ielde tō geoguðe gewęnd wǣre: as though he had been turned from age to youth. Do not mechanically label every wesan+participle a motion perfect.
Dative him is the served person; exact source -ode spelling, not a fabricated finite ending from the infinitive.
Prefixed motion verb with of + dative place left.
Reflexive dative him; ðæs weges is the route genitive, matched by the composition 35.3. Pronoun references need discourse reasoning.
Past participle in āgān wæs, had departed. Distinguish unmacroned āgan began at168.17.
First-person quoted oath; ðurh + accusative oath standard; the narrated speaker now owns ic.
Reflexive mē and adverbial comparison with dyde; this bath verb is supplied, substitute dōn is newly productive.
Exact contracted negative witan lexeme/form is supplied; no full nytan system was taught earlier or is introduced here.
Reflexive hine and tō + dative person toward whom he turned; supply as a local phrase.
The preterite-present knowing verb (§126), not strongI gewītan depart; the dependent question has hwæt ... sīe.
Dative mē is the person served; hyphenation gehīer-/sumode is print line division only.
Mid + dative garment in the passive/predicative description.
Ongēan + tō destination; distinct from wēnan expected despite the similar modern gloss.
Æfter links to the relative antecedent; exact source spelling preserves -odest.
Ðēah concessive clause; hit is the thing withheld. Exact source ending is supplied rather than silently generalized to a weak-II table.
Gegierela is the singular subject, hine the person whose condition is revealed.
Exact source shortened command spelling; the following mixed direct/indirect quotation is explicitly supported by Cook note15, not presented as a regular report transformation.

construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: ðæs weges ðe hē ǣr cōm
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: Source genitive route expression, followed by relative ðe. Apply the bounded genitive-route use taught earlier in this unit, retaining this exact source phrasing and its past-time reference.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: siððan Apollonius āgān wæs
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: After Apollonius had gone away: intransitive completed departure with be, not a passive in which someone sends him away.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: ðurh ðā gemǣnan hǣle
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: Oath by the common safety/salvation; welfare is an explanatory contextual alternative. hǣle is feminine accusative singular of hǣlu, reusing the older exact source form and safety/rescue sense. No possessive our is printed.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: ðurh hwilces geonges mannes ðēnunge ... hwæt se geonga mann sīe
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: The service is the means of the benefit; hwilces ... mannes is its genitive dependent. hwæt asks what sort/status of man he is. sīe is the dependent interrogative be form.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: ēode æfter Apollonio ... ðe ðū æfter āscodest
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: Going after a person, then asking about him: the relative marker is the complement of æfter within the clause; do not force temporal after for either use.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: Ðēah hē hit self forswīge
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: Concessive clause: even if he himself keeps it unspoken. Supply the source forswīge with its present subjunctive interpretation; do not demand a full new weak-verb paradigm.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

construction_notes.label: sęge him ðæt ‘se cyning bitt ðē ðæt ðū cume ...’
construction_notes.actual_supplied_text: Cook note15 explicitly diagnoses mixed direct/reported construction. First him is the messenger’s addressee; within the quoted message ðē is the person invited (accusative), and ðū/cume address him directly. Retain wording and speech levels; no silent repair.
construction_notes.scope_note: Local source reading help only; not a claim of independent productive command of every construction in this phrase.

teaching_records.title: Local forms and constructions in the exact Gymnasium reading

support_cards.explanation: Past participle in passive getǣht wæs; him is the person to whom the route was indicated.
Prefixed movement verb; do not split into an unnoticed new finite gān spelling.
Inside the dependent question hwone ... biddan meahte; indicative/subjunctive surface coincides. The selected interpretation is possibility in the thought.
Exact source prefixed participle and retained w; distinct from selected unprefixed smierwan paradigm. Mid ęle marks the anointing material.
Passive/predicative participle with mid scīetan, a cloth.
Tō + dative bæðstęde identifies what the games/equipment relate to; preserve source note6.
The new productive cry sense; micelre stefne is a dative of manner/instrument.
Exact plural command with shortened -e before following gē, not singular by surface alone. The same form recurs later in the line.
Hine is the person undressed; ðǣm healfan sciccelse is the removed clothing, supplied case frame.
Accusative persons observed; no modern behold quotation formula implied.
On ðæt bæð gives the entry destination.
StrongIII preterite of āginnan, not āgan own/possess and not āgān depart.
Infinitive after began; wið + dative companions and mid + dative ball are supported locally.
Reflexive hine; on ðæs cyninges plegan continues on 169.1. Plegan is an oblique noun governed by on; ðæs cyninges is its genitive possessor. It is not a finite verb.
Joined across printed line break iern-/ende; the supplied participle accompanies Apollonius. Do not count the two printed fragments as two words.
Exact source preterite has short æ as printed; preserve lexical spelling and do not silently import a guessed long form.
Exact accusative participle agreeing with ðone ðoðor, an evidenced exceptional -e form noted by Cook; do not regularize to a new target.
Tō + dative recipient; ongēan is the return direction.
Weak dative modifier of cyninge after ðǣm; the finite paradigm does not itself teach this participial cell.
Exact source singular h spelling; Wright262–263 explicitly gives slōg/slōh. Preserve the earlier selected slōg system and supply this contextual variant.
Accusative snelnesse, followed by a result/content sequence whose pronoun referents remain genuinely underdetermined in Cook note6.
Accusative hine is the praised person; the exact source spelling remains.
New productive selected preterite.
The prefixed verb with tō + dative goal is supplied; do not rename it as the unprefixed nēalǣcan form.

Direct object top is the actual Old English object. The Latin parallel describes rubbing or anointing with ointment; it contains no shoulder or neck noun. Keep that separate event distinct from the Old English.
Supply ðǣm cyninge wæs geðūht swilce ... wǣre, it seemed to the king as though ...; dative experiencer and irrealis comparison are explicit.
In swilce hē of ielde tō geoguðe gewęnd wǣre: as though he had been turned from age to youth. Do not mechanically label every wesan+participle a motion perfect.
Dative him is the served person; exact source -ode spelling, not a fabricated finite ending from the infinitive.
Prefixed motion verb with of + dative place left.
Reflexive dative him; ðæs weges is the route genitive, matched by the composition 35.3. Pronoun references need discourse reasoning.
Past participle in āgān wæs, had departed. Distinguish unmacroned āgan began at168.17.
First-person quoted oath; ðurh + accusative oath standard; the narrated speaker now owns ic.
Reflexive mē and adverbial comparison with dyde; this bath verb is supplied, substitute dōn is newly productive.
Exact contracted negative witan lexeme/form is supplied; no full nytan system was taught earlier or is introduced here.
Reflexive hine and tō + dative person toward whom he turned; supply as a local phrase.
The preterite-present knowing verb (§126), not strongI gewītan depart; the dependent question has hwæt ... sīe.
Dative mē is the person served; hyphenation gehīer-/sumode is print line division only.
Mid + dative garment in the passive/predicative description.
Ongēan + tō destination; distinct from wēnan expected despite the similar modern gloss.
Æfter links to the relative antecedent; exact source spelling preserves -odest.
Ðēah concessive clause; hit is the thing withheld. Exact source ending is supplied rather than silently generalized to a weak-II table.
Gegierela is the singular subject, hine the person whose condition is revealed.
Exact source shortened command spelling; the following mixed direct/indirect quotation is explicitly supported by Cook note15, not presented as a regular report transformation.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: gif hit gelimpð ðæt hē hit finde
support_cards.meaning: if it happens that he finds it
support_cards.explanation: The first hit is impersonal; the second hit is the sheep. Gelimpð is supplied; finde is the newly taught present subjunctive. No full gelimpan person paradigm is assigned.
Gangende accompanies the plural actors hīe. The participial phrase is supplied as a whole; it does not assign a new complete gangan finite system.

support_cards.meaning: Let my books suffice for us both.
support_cards.explanation: Adaptation of the exact167.13 genyhtsumien unc bǣm mīne lȳtlan ǣhta. Books is the verified exercise noun, replacing possessions; plural subject and plural optative stay. Unc is dual dative, bǣm dative plural because both has no separate dual.
Libbendan is the exact supplied weak masculine accusative singular participle agreeing with God after ðone. Existing libban finite tables did not teach this attributive cell.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: on ðā swīðran hand Godes mægenðrymmes
support_cards.meaning: at the right hand of God’s majesty
support_cards.explanation: The source explicitly controls on with accusative. Supply the fixed position expression rather than invent a motion meaning for sitting. The selected perception infinitives sittan/cuman denote the perceived ongoing actions; English -ing is not mechanically converted to an OE participle.

Supply this exact wesan + tō-inflected-infinitive construction for impending coming. Cook§200 supplies the general inflected-infinitive framework, not direct evidence of this particular construction. Personally inspected Matthew16.27 (Kemble/Hardwick132, left column) has ys to cumenne; its apparatus gives A cumanne. The new model selects the already taught is/tō/cumanne spellings, separately from the exact source spelling. Actual prior u06-purpose-infinitive only licenses purpose after a coming verb and does not teach this construction. No general future or necessity system is assigned.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: ðonne āgylt hē ǣlcum be his āgnum weorce
support_cards.meaning: then he rewards everyone according to his own work
support_cards.explanation: Cook prints āgyltan,113. Preserve that original hint in the source; the declared correction is āgyldan, strongIII (§104). BT30b directly gives hē āgylt and dative reward recipient. Supply the entire clause, without claiming a newly taught whole indicative system.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: hū nearu is ðæt geat and se weg ðe tō līfe lǣtt
support_cards.meaning: how narrow is the gate and the way that leads to life
support_cards.explanation: Retain the source’s singular formulation, treating gate and way as the combined figurative route. Supply this exact coordination rather than assigning a blanket singular-agreement rule for coordinated subjects. The nearu adjective table is separately audited by the source editor.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: ne geswāc ðæt hēo mīne fēt ne cyste
support_cards.meaning: did not stop kissing my feet
support_cards.explanation: BT879b quotes WS Luke7.45 with both negatives. The second ne belongs to this attested negative cessation construction; it does not mean that she withheld kisses. Supply the whole finite clause, not just geswīcan or a general complement rule.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: Lǣs lufað ðǣm ðe lǣs forgiefen is.
support_cards.meaning: The one to whom less is forgiven loves less.
support_cards.explanation: The matrix subject is understood from the attracted dative relative. The relative dative belongs to forgiveness; it must not be generalized into a dative subject of ordinary lufian. The prompt attaches neuter accusative singular specifically to its first Less: this is the adverbial degree accusative. The second lǣs is nominative neuter singular, the smaller amount that is forgiven, and is the passive subject. The entire compressed sentence is supplied.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: Hit ne ālīefð ðē hīe tō wīfe habban.
support_cards.meaning: It is not permitted for you to have her as wife.
support_cards.explanation: Impersonal hit with finite ālīefð, dative permitted person ðē, accusative hīe as object of habban, and tō wīfe as the wife-role phrase. Omit the English is; do not add wesan or turn hīe into a dative object.

support_cards.actual_supplied_text: Ðā gehēt hē mid āðe hiere ðæt tō sęllanne, swā hwæs swā hēo hine bǣde.
support_cards.meaning: Then he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked him for.
support_cards.explanation: The promise is expressed by prior gehēt plus the intended-action infinitive. Hiere is the recipient of giving, ðæt the accusative thing given. Internally the free-choice request retains biddan’s genitive thing hwæs and accusative person hine; bǣde is preterite subjunctive in the open request. The resumptive ðæt avoids forcing one relative case to serve incompatible clauses.
The past participle is supplied uninflected in its predicative attachment to hēo; fram plus dative marks the agent. This does not introduce a complete myngian system.

teaching_records.scope_note: Print every assigned help before its task; supplied positions are not tested for unaided recall.

teaching_records.text: Se fæder sægde: ‘Ic eom hēr.’ Se fæder sægde ðæt hē ðǣr wǣre.
teaching_records.translation: The father said, 'I am here.' The father said that he was there.
teaching_records.scope_note: The same speaker becomes third person in a report; here/there assumes that the reporter is speaking from another place.
teaching_records.title: NEW-U16-EXAMPLE-01

teaching_records.text: Hē geseah ðone mann cuman. Hē wiste ðæt se mann cōme.
teaching_records.translation: He saw the man come. He knew that the man came.
teaching_records.scope_note: The perceived actor is accusative with an infinitive; the finite content-clause subject is nominative. The second sentence uses the reported subjunctive.
teaching_records.title: NEW-U16-EXAMPLE-02

teaching_records.text: Gē cunnon ðone cyning; gē cunnon singan.
teaching_records.translation: You know the king; you know how to sing.
teaching_records.scope_note: The new personal-acquaintance sense takes a person as object; the prior skill sense takes a plain infinitive. Witan can also take a person, as Cook35.7 shows; this is not an exclusive lexical partition.
teaching_records.title: NEW-U16-EXAMPLE-03

teaching_records.text: Hē plegode wel, and hīe dydon swā.
teaching_records.translation: He played well, and they did so.
teaching_records.scope_note: Dōn recovers the preceding playing action while retaining its own subject and number.
teaching_records.title: NEW-U16-EXAMPLE-04

U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.

U16-C06-REWARD.inspection_scope: The printed weak headword/class belong to a verb meaning sin or fail in duty. Repay/reward requires the distinct strong gyldan verb. The source English, original hint and original image are all retained; only modern guidance is corrected.

supporting_primary_evidence.observation: Strong a-gildan/-geldan/-gieldan/-gyldan has geald/guldon/golden and includes reward, repay, requite. Separate weak a-giltan has gilte/gilt and means sin, fail, do wrong.
a-gyldan expressly gives thu gyltst/he gylt and geald/guldon/golden. Dative recipients occur in repayment examples. Separate a-gyltan/-giltan has gylte/gilte and gylt/gilt, fail in duty or sin.
Reward is the noun med; requite is forgieldan(III.104). The vocabulary supplies no independent support for agyltan as the verb reward.
Strong gieldan/geald/guldon/golden is explicitly tabulated under104. Prefixing does not turn this into weak class113.
Section113 describes weak de/te preterits retaining the stem vowel, with hieran, fyllan, cyssan, settan and sendan among its examples. It cannot describe strong gyldan/geald/guldon/golden.

review_independence_protocol.blind_phase: Solve every actual learner task from student.md and its visible teaching and support. Earlier accepted learner chapters and actual fifteen-unit registers may be consulted. Initial allowlist: the current learner master, accepted earlier learner materials/registers, original primary images or scans without current editorial annotation, AGENTS.md, EDITORIAL_POLICY.md and this neutral protocol. review_independence_protocol.freeze_gate: Coordinator verifies every actual requested output is attempted, records learner identity, exports Beads and commits the unchanged witness locally. review_independence_protocol.comparison_phase: Compare every frozen solution with the separate key, actual requested output positions, target versus validity distinctions, evidence and exact assigned dependencies.
